meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas. doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.name: mTOR
data.description: Serine/threonine kinase; central regulator of cell growth and metabolism; direct target of rapamycin.
data.description_beginner: The central enzyme this whole Atlas is about - short for 'mechanistic target of rapamycin.' It's a master switch that senses nutrients and growth signals and decides whether a cell should grow, build new proteins, and skip its cleanup routines, or hold back and recycle.

studies.title: mTOR Signaling in Growth, Metabolism, and Disease
studies.authors: Saxton RA; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Comprehensive synthesis of mTORC1/mTORC2 signaling, growth regulation, metabolism, and disease relevance.

studies.title: RAFT1: a mammalian protein that binds to FKBP12 in a rapamycin-dependent fashion and is homologous to yeast TORs
studies.authors: Sabatini DM et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Discovery of the protein RAFT1 (today's mTOR) as the direct target of the FKBP12-rapamycin complex; one of three 1994 reports (with Brown et al. and Chiu et al.) that identified mammalian TOR, three years after TOR was found in yeast.

studies.title: Targets for cell cycle arrest by the immunosuppressant rapamycin in yeast
studies.authors: Heitman J; Movva NR; Hall MN

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Discovery of the TOR1 and TOR2 genes in yeast as the targets whose disruption causes rapamycin's cell-cycle-arresting toxicity - the original genetic identification of the TOR pathway.

studies.title: Genetics: influence of TOR kinase on lifespan in C. elegans
studies.authors: Vellai T et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Silencing the single worm TOR gene roughly doubled C. elegans lifespan, showing the longevity role of TOR inhibition is conserved across an enormous evolutionary distance.

studies.title: Regulation of yeast replicative life span by TOR and Sch9 in response to nutrients
studies.authors: Kaeberlein M; Kennedy BK et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: A systematic screen of 564 yeast gene deletions found 10 deletions that extend replicative lifespan; genes of the nutrient-responsive TOR and Sch9 pathways were the most frequent hits (6 of 10).

studies.title: mTOR interacts with raptor to form a nutrient-sensitive complex that signals to the cell growth machinery
studies.authors: Kim DH; Sarbassov DD; Ali SM; King JE; Latek RR; Erdjument-Bromage H; Tempst P; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Discovery of Raptor as the defining partner of mTOR in mTORC1. This is the paper that gives mTORC1 its identity: Raptor is the scaffold that lets mTOR find and phosphorylate its targets (S6K1), and the complex is stabilized under starvation. Companion paper to Hara 2002.

studies.title: Raptor, a binding partner of target of rapamycin (TOR), mediates TOR action
studies.authors: Hara K; Maruki Y; Long X; Yoshino K; Oshiro N; Hidayat S; Tokunaga C; Avruch J; Yonezawa K

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Independent co-discovery of Raptor (same issue of Cell as Kim 2002). Showed Raptor is essential for mTOR to phosphorylate 4E-BP1 and S6K1, and that knocking it down in worms mimics loss of TOR - confirming Raptor as a core, conserved mediator of TOR action.

studies.title: Rictor, a novel binding partner of mTOR, defines a rapamycin-insensitive and raptor-independent pathway that regulates the cytoskeleton
studies.authors: Sarbassov DD; Ali SM; Kim DH; Guertin DA; Latek RR; Erdjument-Bromage H; Tempst P; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Discovery of Rictor and the SECOND mTOR complex, mTORC2. Crucially showed this complex is NOT blocked by rapamycin and does not use Raptor - it controls the cytoskeleton via PKC. This is the paper that split mTOR biology into 'two faces' at the molecular level.

studies.title: Structure of the FKBP12-rapamycin complex interacting with the binding domain of human FRAP
studies.authors: Choi J; Chen J; Schreiber SL; Clardy J

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: The crystal structure that showed HOW rapamycin works at the atomic level: one rapamycin molecule glues two proteins together - FKBP12 and mTOR's FRB domain - by plugging into two hydrophobic pockets at once. A textbook example of a small molecule acting as 'molecular glue' to force protein dimerization.

studies.title: mTOR kinase structure, mechanism and regulation
studies.authors: Yang H; Rudge DG; Koos JD; Vaidialingam B; Yang HJ; Pavletich NP

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Solved the crystal structure of the mTOR kinase itself. Revealed why the active site is so hard to reach - it sits in a deep recess guarded by the FRB domain, which acts as a 'gatekeeper' letting substrates in. This structure explains at the atomic level exactly how FKBP12-rapamycin blocks access, and why activating cancer mutations cluster where they do.

studies.title: GbetaL, a positive regulator of the rapamycin-sensitive pathway required for the nutrient-sensitive interaction between raptor and mTOR
studies.authors: Kim DH; Sarbassov DD; Ali SM; Latek RR; Guntur KVP; Erdjument-Bromage H; Tempst P; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Discovered mLST8 (GbetaL), the third core subunit that clamps onto mTOR's kinase domain and stabilizes the complex. It fine-tunes how tightly Raptor holds mTOR in response to nutrients - a small but essential cog that later turned out to be especially critical for the mTORC2 complex.

studies.title: AIMTOR, a BRET biosensor for live imaging, reveals subcellular mTOR signaling and dysfunctions
studies.authors: Bouquier N; Perroy J; Ollendorff V et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: HEK293 cells; primary hippocampal neurons and muscle cells (mouse); biosensor tool
studies.finding: AIMTOR is a genetically encoded BRET biosensor that reads out mTOR activity live in single cells and in specific subcellular compartments (cytosol, lysosome surface, nucleus, near mitochondria).

studies.title: Urolithin A activates mitophagy via the AMPK-mTOR axis and modulates the gut-ceramide axis to ameliorate cardiac remodeling in HFpEF
studies.authors: Hangyul Song, Chahyeon Yun, Yunju Choi, Wooju Jeong, Yumin Kim, Jaeyoung Kim, Ju-Yeon Lee, Dongryeol Ryu, Sang-Wook Park, Chang-Myung Oh

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Urolithin A ameliorates HFpEF cardiac remodeling in mice by activating AMPK and inhibiting mTOR to restore mitophagic flux, while simultaneously remodeling the gut microbiome-ceramide axis to reduce lipotoxic stress.

studies.title: Astragaloside IV Mitigates Tacrolimus-Induced Chronic Nephrotoxicity by Regulating the mTOR-TFEB-GADD45alpha Pathway
studies.authors: Ping Gao, Xinwei Cheng, Rui Xu, Xinyu Huang, Jianqiao Wang, Maochang Liu, Xiuxun Wu, Xinlei Guan, Yunzhou Chen, Zhenpeng Qiu
studies.journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Astragaloside IV protects against tacrolimus-induced nephrotoxicity by inhibiting mTOR to activate TFEB and restore autophagy, nominating the mTOR-TFEB-GADD45alpha axis as a calcineurin-independent candidate therapeutic target (preclinical; no human data) in TICN.

studies.title: Molecular and metabolic dysregulation of lung cancer in developing anti-tumor activity by gambogic acid mediated mTOR signaling: in vitro and computational study.
studies.authors: Bo S, Liao Y, Chen X, Liu C, Pang J

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Computational (network pharmacology and docking) plus in vitro study: gambogic acid is cytotoxic and pro-apoptotic in A549 lung cancer cells and docks most strongly to AKT and the mTOR effector S6K1 (RPS6KB1). Direct mTOR kinase inhibition was not measured; no in vivo or human data.

studies.title: GPR143, a novel immunohistochemical marker for renal tumors with FLCN/TSC/MTOR-TFE alterations.
studies.authors: Li Q, Singh A, Hu R, Huang J, Shapiro JB

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: GPR143 is a sensitive and specific immunohistochemical biomarker for renal tumors driven by FLCN/TSC/MTOR-TFE pathway alterations, offering a practical diagnostic tool beyond existing ancillary tests.

studies.title: Age-associated decline of Lamtor5 drives immunosenescence and systemic aging via cGAS-mediated paracrine inflammation.
studies.authors: Lv N, Tang Y, Zhang W, Zhang S, Zhang M

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Age-driven loss of Lamtor5, a key lysosomal mTOR activation complex subunit, drives macrophage immunosenescence and systemic aging phenotypes in mice by unleashing cGAS-STING paracrine inflammation; restoring Lamtor5 in aged mice rescued immunosenescence and attenuated systemic ageing phenotypes.

studies.title: LKB1/AMPK deficiency aggravates mitochondrial DNA leakage via mTOR-dependent mitophagy damage in liver injury sensitized by trichloroethylene.
studies.authors: Zhu L, Wan C, Li Z, Fan X, Liu Z

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: LKB1/AMPK deficiency exacerbates trichloroethylene-induced liver injury by impairing mTOR-regulated mitophagy and causing mitochondrial DNA leakage; rapamycin and AMPK activation are protective, nominating the LKB1/AMPK/mTOR axis as a candidate therapeutic target in mice; no human data.

studies.title: Testosterone propionate maintains autophagic flux and mitochondrial integrity via regulation of the LC3B/p62/Beclin-1/mTOR axis in induced liver fibrosis.
studies.authors: Verma S, Vaishnav S, Yadav M, Verma A, Washimkar K

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Testosterone propionate protects against CCl4-induced liver fibrosis by maintaining mTOR-regulated autophagic flux via the LC3B/p62/Beclin-1 axis, preserving mitochondrial integrity; castration worsens fibrosis by impairing this pathway.

studies.title: Notoginsenoside R1 Alleviates Acetaminophen-Induced Liver Injury via MAPK/mTOR-Mediated Autophagy.
studies.authors: Li S, Liu Z, Pan G, Li Y, Lv K
studies.journal: The American Journal of Chinese Medicine

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Notoginsenoside R1 alleviates acetaminophen-induced acute liver injury by activating protective autophagy through MAPK/mTOR pathway modulation, reducing hepatocyte death and oxidative damage.

studies.title: Rapamycin co-exposure fails to reduce cisplatin-induced damage in GC6-spg spermatogonial cell line.
studies.authors: Jibrin A, Mitchell RT, Lopes F

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Rapamycin did not protect a mouse spermatogonial cell line from cisplatin damage in vitro, unlike reports in female fertility models.

studies.title: mTOR regulates memory CD8 T-cell differentiation
studies.authors: Araki K; Ahmed R et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: mTOR is a key regulator of memory CD8 T-cell differentiation; rapamycin enhances memory responses.

studies.title: Sirolimus for angiomyolipoma in tuberous sclerosis complex or lymphangioleiomyomatosis
studies.authors: Bissler JJ; Franz DN et al.
studies.journal: The New England journal of medicine

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Sirolimus shrinks renal angiomyolipomas in tuberous sclerosis / lymphangioleiomyomatosis.

studies.title: Transient rapamycin treatment can increase lifespan and healthspan in middle-aged mice
studies.authors: Bitto A; Kaeberlein M et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: In male mice, a 3-month rapamycin course started in middle age increased life expectancy by up to 60% (high injected dose). In females that dose did not extend lifespan and shifted cancers toward aggressive haematopoietic types; a lower dietary dose raised survival in both sexes.

studies.title: Aging and immortality: quasi-programmed senescence and its pharmacologic inhibition
studies.authors: Blagosklonny MV

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Proposes the 'hyperfunction theory' of aging: TOR signaling, useful in youth, stays switched on into old age and becomes actively damaging.

studies.title: mTOR mediates Wnt-induced epidermal stem cell exhaustion and aging
studies.authors: Castilho RM; Gutkind JS et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Wnt-induced mTOR activation drives epidermal stem-cell senescence; rapamycin rescues it.

studies.title: The mTOR kinase differentially regulates effector and regulatory T cell lineage commitment
studies.authors: Delgoffe GM; Powell JD et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: T cells lacking mTOR fail to become normal effector cells and default toward regulatory T cells, showing mTOR is a master switch for immune cell fate.

studies.title: Rapamycin decelerates cellular senescence
studies.authors: Demidenko ZN; Zubova SG; Bukreeva EI; Pospelov VA; Pospelova TV; Blagosklonny MV

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Blagosklonny's key experiment behind his 'hyperfunction' theory of aging. When a cell's division is blocked but mTOR keeps driving growth, the cell tips into permanent senescence. Rapamycin uncouples the two - keeping arrested cells reversible instead of senescent. Direct evidence that mTOR actively drives the senescent state, not just passively accompanies it.

studies.title: Late-life rapamycin treatment reverses age-related heart dysfunction
studies.authors: Flynn JM; O'Leary MN; Zambataro CA; Academia EC; Presley MP; et al.; Melov S

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Striking evidence that in mice mTOR inhibition doesn't just SLOW aging - it can partly reverse an established age-related phenotype. Giving rapamycin to already-old (24-month) female mice for 3 months improved aged heart function, reversing or attenuating age-related cardiac changes, with RNA-seq changes suggesting anti-hypertrophic and anti-inflammatory effects. Started late, still worked.

studies.title: Mice fed rapamycin have an increase in lifespan associated with major changes in the liver transcriptome
studies.authors: Fok WC; Richardson A et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Rapamycin-fed mice show extended lifespan with major changes in the liver transcriptome.

studies.title: Efficacy and safety of everolimus for subependymal giant cell astrocytomas associated with tuberous sclerosis complex (EXIST-1): a multicentre, randomised, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial
studies.authors: Franz DN; Belousova E; Sparagana S; Bebin EM; Frost M; et al.; Jozwiak S

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Phase 3 RCT (n=117) in tuberous sclerosis, the disease where mTOR is stuck ON by a genetic fault. Everolimus shrank brain tumors (SEGA) by >=50% in 35% of patients versus 0% on placebo. Because the underlying cause here is direct mTOR overactivation, this is arguably the cleanest randomised human evidence that blocking mTOR works in a genetically defined mTORopathy -- which does not extend to mTOR inhibition in people without such a mutation.

studies.title: A diverse array of cancer-associated MTOR mutations are hyperactivating and can predict rapamycin sensitivity
studies.authors: Grabiner BC; Sabatini DM et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: A spectrum of cancer-associated MTOR mutations are hyperactivating and predict rapamycin sensitivity.

studies.title: Defining the role of mTOR in cancer
studies.authors: Guertin DA; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Comprehensive review arguing mTOR signaling is commonly deregulated in human cancers, laying out the rationale for rapalog trials in oncology.

studies.title: mTOR Signaling Confers Resistance to Targeted Cancer Drugs
studies.authors: Guri Y; Hall MN et al.

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Review of how mTOR signalling confers resistance to targeted cancer therapies.

studies.title: Chronic inhibition of mTOR by rapamycin modulates cognitive and non-cognitive components of behavior throughout lifespan in mice
studies.authors: Halloran J; Hussong SA; Burbank R; Podlutskaya N; Fischer KE; et al.; Galvan V

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Asked whether the lifespan-extending dose of rapamycin harms or helps the aging BRAIN. Reassuringly, it enhanced learning and memory in young mice, prevented age-related cognitive decline in old ones, and even reduced anxiety and depression-like behavior - linked to boosted brain monoamines. Cognitive benefit, not cost.

studies.title: What is the clinical evidence to support off-label rapamycin therapy in healthy adults?
studies.authors: Hands JM; Lustgarten MS; Frame LA; Rosen B

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Narrative review + PhenoAge modeling of one cohort
studies.finding: A deliberately cautious review of low-dose rapamycin in healthy adults, and re-models one cohort using the PhenoAge biological-aging clock. Verdict: despite strong animal lifespan data, human evidence does NOT yet prove rapamycin delays aging in healthy people. A valuable counterweight to longevity-community hype - it holds the human evidence to a strict standard rather than over-reading promising signals.

studies.title: Rapamycin fed late in life extends lifespan in genetically heterogeneous mice
studies.authors: Harrison DE et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Rapamycin fed from 600 days of age extended median and maximal lifespan in both sexes; age at 90% mortality rose 14% in females and 9% in males.

studies.title: Temsirolimus, interferon alfa, or both for advanced renal-cell carcinoma
studies.authors: Hudes G et al.

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Temsirolimus alone extended median overall survival to 10.9 months versus 7.3 months with interferon alfa in poor-prognosis metastatic kidney cancer; rash, hyperglycemia, and hyperlipidemia were more common with temsirolimus.

studies.title: mTOR is a key modulator of ageing and age-related disease
studies.authors: Johnson SC; Rabinovitch PS; Kaeberlein M

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: The landmark Nature review that put mTOR at the center of aging biology. Lays out the case that inhibiting mTOR extends lifespan across species and guards against a growing list of age-related diseases - while being candid that side effects currently block its use in healthy people. Excellent orientation map for the whole field.

studies.title: Efficacy of sirolimus compared with azathioprine for reduction of acute renal allograft rejection: a randomised multicentre study
studies.authors: Kahan BD (Rapamune US Study Group)

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: The trial that established rapamycin (sirolimus) as an immunosuppressant in kidney transplant patients - its original, still-standard clinical use.

studies.title: The Mechanistic Target of Rapamycin: The Grand ConducTOR of Metabolism and Aging
studies.authors: Kennedy BK; Lamming DW

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: A Cell Metabolism review framing mTOR as the 'grand conductor' that coordinates whole-body metabolism, tissue by tissue. Especially valuable for its clear-eyed section on WHY rapamycin causes metabolic side effects (the mTORC2 problem) - which is the main barrier to using it against aging. Pairs perfectly with Lamming's own 2012 mechanism paper.

studies.title: Everolimus for subependymal giant-cell astrocytomas in tuberous sclerosis
studies.authors: Krueger DA et al.

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: In patients whose TSC1/TSC2 mutations cause brain tumors, everolimus shrank tumor volume by 30%+ in three-quarters of patients. Open-label and uncontrolled (n=28); randomised confirmation came later (FRA2013).

studies.title: Targeting ageing with rapamycin and its derivatives in humans: a systematic review
studies.authors: Lee DJW; Hodzic Kuerec A; Maier AB

evidence.label: Synthesis of human data
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: The first systematic review of rapamycin/rapalogs in humans for aging. Screened 18,400 articles, included 19 studies. Found improvements in immune, cardiovascular, and skin (integumentary) parameters; NO significant effect on endocrine, muscular, or neurological systems. No serious adverse events in healthy people, but more infections and raised cholesterol/triglycerides in people with age-related disease. This is the highest-tier human-evidence summary in the whole Atlas - it aggregates many individual human studies rather than reporting one.

studies.title: mTOR at the nexus of nutrition, growth, ageing and disease
studies.authors: Liu GY; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: The flagship modern review of the whole field, from Sabatini's own lab (Nature Reviews Molecular Cell Biology). Maps 25+ years of mTOR biology - how it senses nutrients, controls growth and autophagy, and goes wrong in cancer, neurodegeneration, metabolic disease and aging. The single best orientation document for the entire Atlas.

studies.title: mTOR-dependent synapse formation underlies the rapid antidepressant effects of NMDA antagonists
studies.authors: Li N; Duman RS et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Ketamine's rapid antidepressant action requires mTOR-dependent synaptogenesis in prefrontal cortex.

studies.title: Targeting the biology of ageing with mTOR inhibitors to improve immune function in older adults: phase 2b and phase 3 randomised trials
studies.authors: Mannick JB; Teo G; Bernardo P; Quinn D; Russell K; Klickstein L; Marshall W; Shergill S

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: The crucial reality check. After the promising phase 2a, the large phase 3 trial (n=1024) FAILED its primary endpoint - RTB101 did not reduce clinically symptomatic respiratory illness (26% vs 25%, p=0.65). It still reliably switched on antiviral genes, so the biomarker moved but the clinical outcome did not. A textbook lesson that a promising biomarker is not a proven benefit.

studies.title: Efficacy and safety of sirolimus in lymphangioleiomyomatosis (MILES)
studies.authors: McCormack FX; Inoue Y; Moss J; Singer LG; Strange C; et al.; Trapnell BC

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: A landmark placebo-controlled RCT (n=89) - the first to show that rapamycin (sirolimus) benefits a human lung disease. In LAM, lung function normally declines relentlessly; sirolimus STOPPED that decline while patients took it (and it resumed after stopping). Randomised human evidence that mTOR inhibition can suspend progression of this disease; the benefit did not persist after withdrawal.

studies.title: Rapamycin, but not resveratrol or simvastatin, extends life span of genetically heterogeneous mice
studies.authors: Miller RA; Harrison DE et al.
studies.journal: J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: In the same experimental design that showed rapamycin extended median lifespan by 10-18%, neither resveratrol nor simvastatin had any significant effect on survival - a direct head-to-head negative control run at the same time, in the same mice.

studies.title: Rapamycin-mediated lifespan increase in mice is dose and sex dependent and metabolically distinct from dietary restriction
studies.authors: Miller RA; Strong R et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Rapamycin's lifespan extension in mice is dose-dependent and greater in females.

studies.title: Influence of rapamycin on safety and healthspan metrics after one year: PEARL trial results
studies.authors: Moel M; Harinath G; Lee V; Nyquist A; Morgan SL; Isman A; Zalzala S

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: First completed long-term RCT of rapamycin for healthy human aging (NCT04488601, 48 weeks, n=114). Primary endpoint (visceral fat by DXA) showed NO significant change (p=0.942) - a null result on the pre-registered primary endpoint. Secondary endpoints were more promising: women on the 10mg/week dose had significant improvements in lean tissue mass and self-reported pain. A textbook example of why the pre-registered primary endpoint, not the most exciting secondary finding, is what should drive the headline conclusion.

studies.title: mTOR signalling and cellular metabolism are mutual determinants in cancer
studies.authors: Mossmann D; Hall MN et al.

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Review of mTOR and cellular metabolism as mutual determinants in cancer.

studies.title: Rapamycin extends murine lifespan but has limited effects on aging
studies.authors: Neff F; Ehninger D et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Rapamycin extends murine lifespan but has only limited effects on classic aging phenotypes.

studies.title: Regulation of immune responses by mTOR
studies.authors: Powell JD; Horton MR et al.

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Review of mTOR as an integrator of immune-cell metabolism and differentiation.

studies.title: Overcoming mTOR resistance mutations with a new-generation mTOR inhibitor
studies.authors: Rodrik-Outmezguine VS; Shokat KM et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: RapaLink-1, a third-generation bivalent inhibitor, overcomes mTOR resistance mutations.

studies.title: Twenty-five years of mTOR: Uncovering the link from nutrients to growth
studies.authors: Sabatini DM
studies.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Sabatini's 25-year synthesis linking nutrient sensing to growth through mTOR.

studies.title: A randomized controlled trial to establish effects of short-term rapamycin treatment in 24 middle-aged companion dogs
studies.authors: Urfer SR; Kaeberlein M et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: A short 10-week course of low-dose rapamycin in healthy pet dogs caused no clinical side effects, and echocardiography suggested improved measures of heart function.

studies.title: Activating mTOR mutations in a patient with an extraordinary response on a phase I trial of everolimus and pazopanib
studies.authors: Wagle N; Rosenberg JE et al.

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Two concurrent activating MTOR mutations are implicated in an extraordinary clinical response to rapalog therapy. Single-patient observation: hypothesis-generating, not evidence of a general response predictor.

studies.title: Rapamycin slows aging in mice
studies.authors: Wilkinson JE; Burmeister L; Brooks SV; Chan CC; Friedline S; Harrison DE; Hejtmancik JF; Nadon N; Strong R; Wood LK; Woodward MA; Miller RA

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Answered a crucial objection: does rapamycin really slow AGING, or just prevent the cancers that kill mice? By showing slower age-related change across many tissues (heart, liver, tendon, activity), it argued for genuine slowing of aging. Honestly reported harms too - more cataracts and testicular degeneration - making it a balanced landmark, not hype.

studies.title: Nutrient-sensing pathways in adult stem cells: Orchestrating homeostasis, aging, and disease
studies.authors: Xiao T; Zeng YA; Hu C et al.

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Review (adult stem cells, multiple tissue systems)
studies.finding: Proposes an integrated framework in which mTOR, AMPK, sirtuins, and insulin/IGF-1 signaling jointly govern adult stem cell transitions between quiescence, activation, and differentiation; age-related dysregulation of this nutrient-sensing network drives stem cell exhaustion and tissue degeneration, and interventions (mTOR inhibitors, AMPK activators, NAD+ precursors, dietary strategies) can restore ASC function.

studies.title: Deubiquitinase USP7 stabilizes the histone demethylase KDM5B and promotes the progression of renal fibrosis through the TSC1/mTOR axis
studies.authors: Lv S; Zhang Xiaoyan et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Mouse (UUO and unilateral renal ischemia-reperfusion injury models); human CKD kidney tissue (correlative)
studies.finding: USP7 deubiquitinates and stabilizes the histone demethylase KDM5B, which represses TSC1 transcription and thereby activates mTOR, promoting kidney fibrosis in two mouse injury models; USP7 is upregulated in human CKD kidneys and correlates with fibrosis severity. Genetic or pharmacological USP7 inhibition restores TSC1 expression, suppresses mTOR activation, and attenuates fibrosis in these mice, making the USP7-KDM5B-TSC1-mTOR axis a candidate intervention point; the human data are correlative only.

studies.title: Diet-dependent, beneficial and adverse effects of rapamycin on life span of Drosophila melanogaster
studies.authors: Jackson LN; Boles AM; Frye CT; Patel IA; Mockett RJ

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Rapamycin's effect on Drosophila lifespan is highly diet-dependent: on a cornmeal/torula-yeast medium it was harmful in 19 of 26 experiments across 5 strains, but on a nutrient-rich brewer's-yeast medium it was beneficial in 8 and neutral in 14, with no significant harm. Effects on median lifespan ranged from -51.3% to +5.4%, varying by sex and strain; rapamycin was also toxic to development at 10-200 µM.

studies.title: mTOR inhibition augments antitumor immune effector response by reprogramming the TP53-mutant, immune-cold HNSCC tumor microenvironment
studies.authors: Nath P; Khandelwal A; Li C; Moore-Medlin T; Vasudevan SS; Alvarez VA; Franco OE; Gutkind JS; Nathan CO

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Syngeneic mouse models of TP53-mutant HNSCC
studies.finding: In syngeneic TP53-mutant HNSCC mouse models, the mTOR inhibitor everolimus reprogrammed the immune-cold tumor microenvironment: it increased CD8+ T cell and dendritic cell infiltration, reduced Tregs and HIF-1α/VEGFA-driven MDSC recruitment, boosted TNF-α/CXCL10 chemokine signaling, and reduced PD-1/PD-L1 expression — restoring T-cell cytotoxic competence and suppressing tumor growth.

studies.title: Survival and Homeostasis of Alveolar Macrophages in Vivo Depend on mTOR Signaling
studies.authors: Hennessy-Strahs S; Su X; Sun S; Deng G; Muo W; Li Jiarui; Miller T; Xiao X; Li XC
studies.journal: American Journal of Respiratory Cell and Molecular Biology

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Mouse (myeloid-specific Mtor deletion); GM-CSF-driven alveolar-macrophage-like cell culture (in vitro)
studies.finding: Myeloid-specific deletion of mTOR (and pharmacologic mTOR inhibition with temsirolimus) causes progressive depletion of alveolar macrophages, impaired phagocytosis, lipid accumulation and PAP-like lung pathology in mice, identifying mTOR as a nonredundant regulator of alveolar macrophage survival — mechanistic support for mTOR-inhibitor-associated pulmonary toxicity.

studies.title: Fluorescent protein ticker tape (FPTT): Multiplexed recording of transcriptional dynamics in living cells and in vivo
studies.authors: Wang R; Jiang J et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: HEK293T cells, synchronised (live recording of mTOR-driven transcription, SREBP1 response element)
studies.finding: Engineered a multiplexed fluorescent-protein 'ticker tape' biosensor platform (self-assembling protein fibers + multispectral fluorescent proteins) for longitudinal, single-cell recording of signaling-pathway transcriptional histories (mTOR, NF-κB, STAT3, NFAT, cAMP). Applying the mTOR-FPTT reporter, the authors independently observed cell-cycle-dependent OSCILLATING mTOR activity dynamics -- a new, orthogonal tool corroborating that mTOR signaling is patterned over time rather than static, consistent with JOS2024's cell-cycle oscillation finding.

studies.title: Aberrant Proteostasis of BMAL1 Underlies Circadian Abnormalities in a Paradigmatic mTOR-opathy
studies.authors: Lipton JO; Boyle LM; Yuan ED; Hochstrasser KJ; Chifamba FF; Nathan A; Tsai PT; Davis F; Sahin M

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Mouse models of tuberous sclerosis complex (Tsc1/Tsc2 loss)
studies.finding: In mouse models of tuberous sclerosis, where mTOR is stuck on, the circadian clock ran abnormally: poor timekeeping in constant conditions and exaggerated responses to phase resetting. mTOR raised BMAL1 levels by changing its translation, degradation and location; genetically lowering BMAL1 rescued the behavioural rhythm defects. Constant, unpatterned mTOR activity disturbs a rhythm downstream.

studies.title: mTOR signaling regulates central and peripheral circadian clock function
studies.authors: Ramanathan C; Kathale ND; Liu D; Lee C; Freeman DA; Hogenesch JB; Cao R; Liu AC

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Hepatocyte and adipocyte clock models; Tsc2-/- fibroblasts; ex vivo SCN and liver; mTOR heterozygous mice
studies.finding: mTOR sets how fast and how strongly the circadian clock ticks. Inhibiting mTOR lengthened the clock period and flattened its amplitude; activating it shortened the period and raised the amplitude, in cells, in ex vivo brain (SCN) and liver clocks, and in mTOR heterozygous mice, whose locomotor rhythm ran longer. The study starts from the observation that mTOR activity itself oscillates over 24 hours in many tissues.

studies.title: Circadian regulation of mTOR by the ubiquitin pathway in renal cell carcinoma
studies.authors: Okazaki H; Matsunaga N; Fujioka T; Okazaki F; Akagawa Y; Tsurudome Y; Ono M; Kuwano M; Koyanagi S; Ohdo S

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: In mouse kidney tumours, active phosphorylated mTOR and total mTOR protein followed a 24-hour rhythm, set by the clock through the ubiquitin ligase Fbxw7. Giving everolimus when mTOR was high improved survival compared with other dosing times. Same drug, same dose - the clock time of dosing changed the outcome.

relations.mechanism: DEPTOR sits on mTOR and damps both complexes; myeloma cells overexpress it and depend on that damping.
relations.mechanism_beginner: DEPTOR sits on mTOR and dampens both complexes; some cancer cells (myeloma) make extra DEPTOR and come to depend on that damping.

relations.mechanism: mTORC2 is built around the same mTOR kinase as mTORC1 - the partner subunits, not the catalytic core, are what make the two complexes different.
relations.mechanism_beginner: mTORC2 is built from the very same mTOR enzyme as mTORC1 – it's the partner proteins around it that make the two complexes different.
relations.note: Three independent structures - unusually well supported for this corpus.
